claude_only.name: Which system is the master of record for this run's identifier, and what is the exact literal form of that identifier?
When the executing provider returns no run identifier, what identifier does the adopting Dimension mint, and how is uniqueness guaranteed?
Does the identifier stay stable across retries, streaming resumption and later asynchronous result retrieval, or does each attempt receive a new one?
Which vendor-native identifiers are retained beside the authoritative identifier, and what is each one good for?
Which trace identifier and span identifier bind this run into the surrounding distributed trace, and in which propagation format?
Which conversation, session or thread identifier groups this run with the runs that preceded and followed it?
How are correlation keys preserved when the run crosses a process, vendor or network boundary?
What is recorded when the trace is not sampled, telemetry is dropped, or no conversation exists for this operation type?
Which operation type does this run represent, drawn from a closed and versioned code list?
Was the run synchronous, streaming, batched or asynchronously retrieved, and where exactly do its temporal boundaries fall?
Does this run represent a single model call or an agentic loop that may contain many model and tool calls?
Under which regulatory regime and which risk category is the AI system performing this run classified, and by whose determination?
Does the applicable regime impose a minimum log content set for runs of this class, and is every mandated element actually present?
What degree of human oversight must be exercised over runs of this class before their effects take hold?
Which jurisdictions' obligations apply to this run, given where it executed and where its effects land?
What exactly was presented to the model as system instructions, chat history, prompt variables and attachments?
Is verbatim input content captured, and under which opt-in, truncation, filtering or sampling rule was that decided?
Where content is too large or is binary, how is it externalised and referenced back from the run record?
How can the exact input be reconstructed later if the referenced payload store has since changed?
For each input segment, what is its origin - end user, retrieved document, tool result, upstream agent or system operator?
Which input segments were treated as untrusted data that must never be interpreted as instructions?
How is a suspected prompt-injection or untrusted-instruction attempt recorded against the run?
Which model was requested and which model identifier actually produced the response?
Which provider, endpoint address and serving region handled the run?
Which model version, snapshot or inference profile is recorded so a later reader knows which weights answered?
Can this run be re-executed to produce an identical result, and what specifically prevents bit-identical reproduction?
How is a parameter recorded when the provider has deprecated, capped or silently ignored it for the selected model?
Which configuration snapshot does the run reference, and is that snapshot immutable and content-addressed?
Which tools, resources and data sources were offered to the model at run start, and in which order were they presented?
Which authorization scopes and resource indicators bounded what the run could reach?
Did the available capability set change during the run, and how is each change point recorded?
How is the run decomposed into ordered steps, and what identifies each step uniquely within the run?
What parent-child relationships hold between orchestration steps, model-call steps and tool-call steps?
Are intermediate reasoning or planning outputs captured, and under which disclosure and retention rule?
How many model calls and tool calls did the run make, and were any iteration limits reached?
For each tool call, which tool on which server was invoked, with which arguments, and what did it return?
Did the call fail at protocol level or return an execution error, and how is that distinction preserved in the record?
What side-effect character did the tool declare - read-only, destructive, idempotent, open-world - and was that declaration treated as trusted?
How are retries, timeouts, cancellations and input-required round trips of the same logical call linked together?
Which data sources or knowledge bases were queried to ground this run's output?
Which specific retrieved items entered the model context, and can each be re-resolved at the version that was used?
How fresh and how authoritative was the retrieved content at the instant it was used?
Which sub-runs or delegated agent invocations did this run spawn, and in which order?
On whose authority did each sub-agent act, and was the granted authority narrowed at every delegation hop?
How are the cost, failure and output of a sub-run rolled up into the parent without double counting?
What terminates a delegation chain, and what prevents unbounded recursion or fan-out?
What is the complete set of run states, and which transitions between them are legal?
In which state did the run terminate, and for what stated reason?
How is a partially completed or truncated run distinguished from an outright failure for audit purposes?
Which low-cardinality error type is recorded when the run ends in error, and where does the full diagnostic live?
What are the run's start and end instants, and in which format and offset are they expressed?
How is the instant at which the run occurred distinguished from the instants at which it was observed, ingested and billed?
Which latency measures are recorded, and from whose vantage point are they measured?
Which clock source produced these instants, and what skew is tolerated before ordering becomes unreliable?
Which content blocks did the run produce, in which modalities and in which order?
Was the output schema-constrained, and did it validate against the declared output schema?
How is the output stored, digested and referenced so a later reader can prove what was actually returned?
Which parts of the output were presented to a human, and which were consumed only by downstream machinery?
For each media asset produced, is a signed provenance manifest attached, and which assertions does it carry?
Is the asset marked as AI-generated using a recognised digital source type, and does that marking survive downstream processing?
How is the manifest bound back to this run and to the ingredients that were consumed to create the asset?
Which principal initiated this run, and whose credentials were presented against each downstream resource?
Which scopes were granted, and was each access token bound to the specific resource it was used against?
Where the agent acted on behalf of a person or organisation, how is that on-behalf-of chain recorded?
How is an end user identified in the run record without persisting direct personal identifiers?
Which actions in this run required explicit human approval before they could execute?
Who approved or denied each gated action, at what instant, and what information were they shown at the time?
Was the run paused, stopped or overridden by a human, and what effect did that have on the trajectory?
How is a missing but required approval detected, escalated and recorded as a non-conformity?
Which provenance classes and properties does this run map to, and what are the resolvable IRIs for its activity and agents?
Who owns the run record, and who is the accountable deployer answerable for the run's effects?
Which outputs were derived from which inputs and retrieved items, and is that derivation edge explicit rather than inferred?
Under which tenant, workspace, project or cost centre is this run attributed?
How many input, output, cache-read, cache-creation and reasoning tokens did the run consume?
Which non-token resources were consumed, and how is that set enumerated for this operation type?
How are provider-reported counts reconciled with locally computed counts when the two disagree?
Into which measurement time bucket is usage assigned when the run spans a bucket boundary?
What monetary cost is attributed to this run, in which currency and against which price basis?
Is the recorded cost a local estimate or an authoritative billed amount, and how is that status flagged and later upgraded?
To which API key, workspace, service tier and cost centre is this run's cost charged?
How are sub-run costs and cached-token savings allocated so that nothing is counted twice?
Which evaluations were performed against this run's output, by which evaluator and at which evaluator version?
What score, label or verdict did each evaluation produce, and on what scale is it interpretable?
Was the evaluation performed inline during the run or asynchronously afterwards, and how late may it still arrive?
How is human feedback on the run captured and kept distinguishable from automated evaluation?
Which policy or guardrail checks were applied to this run's inputs, intermediate steps and outputs?
What did each check decide - allow, transform or block - and what exactly was modified?
Which policy version was in force at the instant of each decision?
How is a blocked or refused run evidenced without persisting the prohibited content itself?
Which regulated minimum log elements must this run's record contain, and is each one demonstrably present?
For how long must the record be kept, counted from which start point, and on which legal basis?
Who holds the logs when provider and deployer differ, and how is the phrase under their control demonstrated?
How are erasure requests, legal holds and statutory minimum-retention duties reconciled when they conflict?
What exactly is destroyed at end of life, and what tombstone remains to prove the record once existed?
How is the run record sealed at close so that any later alteration becomes detectable?
Which fields become immutable when the run closes, and which may still legitimately be appended afterwards?
How is a correction recorded without overwriting the original assertion?
Who can verify the seal, against which trust anchor, and what happens when verification fails?
Who may read run inputs and outputs, as opposed to run metadata and measures only?
Which fields are classified as sensitive, and what masking or truncation applies by default?
Which accesses to the run record must themselves be logged, and what does that access log capture?
Which residency or cross-border constraints bind the record, and how do they differ from the constraints on the inference itself?
Into which external schemas can a run record be projected, and which profile governs each projection?
Which fields have no target in a given external schema, and how is that loss declared to the consumer?
How are vendor-specific attributes carried without polluting the canonical model?
How is an imported third-party run record marked as externally asserted rather than locally observed?

grok_only.name: What authoritative master-system identifier did the inference or agent runtime assign to this execution?
If no provider master identifier exists, what UUID or ULID did the adopting Dimension assign, and why was a master identifier absent?
Which pre-existing conversation, session or thread identifier correlates this run, and was it supplied by the instrumented system rather than minted as a fallback?
Does this run continue a prior response or interaction, and what previous-response identifier was passed as context?
What W3C trace-id and span-id identify this run, and is the sampled flag set?
Which parent execution, if any, contains this run, and which child spans did this run generate?
How is this trace context propagated across HTTP or other carriers so vendor traces can be joined?
Were all-zero or non-random trace identifiers rejected rather than stored as valid run identity?
Which well-known or custom operation name classifies this run, and does a predefined OpenTelemetry value apply?
Which GenAI provider name did instrumentation record, and does it identify a proxy rather than the upstream model vendor?
What OpenInference span kind, if any, is recorded alongside the OpenTelemetry operation, and where do the two classifications disagree?
Is this run an ISO/IEC 22989 inference process, an inference result, an agent activity, or a non-inferential fetch of a stored response?
What exact model name did the caller request?
What exact model name did the provider report as having generated the response?
If an agent can select among multiple models, was a single request.model omitted on the agent span as required?
Which governed configuration object records the allowed model routing that this run actually used?
What are the RFC 3339 event start and event end of this logical operation, including any automatic retries?
When was this run record observed or ingested into the governed store, if that instant differs from event time?
Does this run satisfy the Article 12 duty to record the period of each use, and is the system in a high-risk class that makes that field mandatory?
What PROV activity start and end times, and optional usage or generation times, are asserted for this run?
Was this request issued in streaming mode, and if unset is non-streaming correctly assumed?
What was the time in seconds from request issuance to first streamed chunk?
What client or server operation duration was recorded for this run, and in which UCUM unit?
In what terminal state did this run end, and which finish reasons did the model or agent report?
If the run failed, what error.type or exception type, message and stack were recorded?
Did a content filter, guardrail, refusal or max-token length stop generation, and is that encoded as a finish reason rather than a silent truncation?
Is this run still open, completed, cancelled, timed out, or awaiting human oversight before it may close?
Were transient automatic retries folded into this logical run, and how many attempts occurred?
Was the run cancelled or terminated by timeout before a model finish reason was produced?
Was the effective conversation context a compacted view of a prior conversation, and was the compacted attribute left unset rather than set to false when unknown?
Is this a fetch of a stored response without inference, and were token usage attributes and metrics omitted as required?
What ordered input messages and roles were provided to the model, and were they truncated or filtered?
Were system instructions supplied separately from chat history, and what is their content or content hash?
Which named prompt and version were used, and what variable values were substituted?
What MIME type, modalities and output type did the client request?
What output messages or choices were returned, and which finish reason applies to each?
Were reasoning, encrypted or redacted thinking blocks returned, and are vendor signatures preserved for replay without logging plaintext chain-of-thought?
What integrity hash or external URI identifies the canonical output payload used for later audit or evaluation?
Was content captured inline, truncated, hashed only, redacted, streamed as chunks, or uploaded to external storage?
What personal data or sensitive classes were detected in inputs or outputs, and which redaction rules applied?
Who is authorised to read unredacted payloads for this run, and under which access exception?
Is the captured payload complete enough to reproduce or evaluate the run, and what completeness or integrity evidence exists?
Which stable executing agent identifier, name and version performed this run?
Which PROV association, attribution or delegation links this activity to the responsible agent, organisation or human overseer?
Which exact configuration identifiers were in force for prompts, tools, decoding, routing and safety policy?
Which organisation, deployer or system owner is accountable for this execution?
Which tool definitions were advertised to the model or agent for this run?
Which tool calls were executed, with what call identifiers, arguments, results, duration and error type?
Under what authority, allow-list or human approval was each tool allowed to run, especially for side-effecting tools?
Were multiple tool calls issued in parallel, and how are their identifiers kept distinct in the trace?
Which data sources were queried, with what query, top-k and retrieved document identifiers and scores?
Which memory store operations ran during this execution, and which memory records were created, searched, updated or deleted?
Did the agent emit a distinct plan or task-decomposition phase, and what plan artifact was produced?
Which nested agent or workflow invocations were spawned, and how do they reference their parent run without minting new agent entities?
Are the recorded token counts billed units, consumed units, or both, and which value is canonical for charging?
How many input tokens were cache reads or cache writes, and how many output tokens were reasoning tokens?
What text, image and audio token counts were reported, and do they sum consistently into the totals?
How many nested inference calls and tool calls did this agent invocation make, and what were their token totals?
Was a monetary cost recorded for this run, in what currency, and which schema supplied the fields?
How is cost split across prompt, completion, cache, reasoning and audio details?
If only tokens are available, is cost left unset rather than inferred from an unofficial rate card?
Which billing account, project or tenant is charged for this run without importing the invoice object?
What server address and port did the client observe for this GenAI operation, behind intermediaries if known?
Does the recorded server address support a data-residency inference, or is residency unknown and therefore unset?
Was the call relayed through a gateway or proxy, and does provider.name therefore differ from the upstream vendor?
Is this run in scope of EU high-risk automatic logging, of a voluntary NIST monitoring programme, or only of operational tracing?
Which Article 12 minimum fields (use period, reference database, matched inputs, verifying persons) are present on this run?
Are the automatically generated logs under provider control, deployer control, or both, and where is the authoritative copy?
Can this log identify a risk situation, substantial modification, or operational anomaly required for post-market monitoring?
What retention period applies to this run's metadata versus its payload content, and which legal basis sets each period?
If a data-subject erasure request applies, was payload content deleted or anonymised while the audit skeleton was retained?
Is the run under legal hold, incident investigation or competent-authority request that suspends deletion?
When and by whom was the run or its payloads deleted, and what evidence remains of the deletion?
Which natural persons or roles verified, approved, overrode or rejected the result of this run?
What oversight decision was taken, at what event time, and did it alter the output that downstream systems consumed?
Which user or subject initiated the run, and is that identity a verified person, an application, or another agent?
Did oversight suspend further use because the system may present an Article 79 risk?
What quality, safety or task evaluations were attached to this run, with which scores, labels and annotator kinds?
Was an independent reviewer used, and is the evaluation itself attributed as a PROV bundle?
What integrity hash, signature or chain links this run record to previous audit records so post-hoc modification is detectable?
What security controls prevent prompt, tool-argument or secret leakage through telemetry exporters?
What default access rule applies to this run's metadata versus its payloads?
What exception, ticket or competent-authority request granted broader access, and is that access itself audited?
Which interoperability profile was used to export this run, and which competing fields were mapped rather than treated as equivalent?
Was this run sampled out of full telemetry, and does sampling still satisfy the applicable logging duty?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
